title: Egypt: narcotics received and dispensed book
notice: A starting point, not certified for the country. Check each column against the instrument before you rely on it. Read from Law 182/1960 as first published (Official Gazette No. 131, 13 June 1960): six later amending laws were not traced, so confirm Art. 18 against the current text before printing into the book. The law sets no way to correct an entry: this set takes the strictest, a reversing line. The patient's age and the prescriptions-book entry number print empty until the register reads them: write them in. Art. 18 asks for the quantity of narcotic a dispensed medicine contains; the book prints the quantity dispensed in the item's unit, so put the narcotic content in the item's name. The six-monthly statement (Art. 23) is not set up yet, nor the prescriptions book (Arts. 17, 18(c)), for which the law lists no fields.
sources: Law No. 182 of 1960 on narcotics, Official Gazette No. 131, 13 June 1960: Arts. 17, 18, 23, 31 (gazette pp. 964-966, the scan on edaegypt.gov.eg)

books.title: Narcotics received and dispensed book
books.cite: Law 182/1960 Art. 18: entered on the day received and on the day dispensed, in a book whose pages are numbered and sealed by the authority; kept 10 years from the last entry, Art. 31
books.medium_note: Pages numbered and sealed by the competent authority (Art. 18): print into that book, in clear letters, following its own page numbers.
